inputs.original_text: Bloomberg: “Every day, as energy prices rise, flights are canceled and death and destruction fill screens, people across the world ask when the Iran war — widely viewed as poorly planned, unwinnable and a peril to global well-being — will stop.” “Not in Israel, where the public is strongly behind seeing the war through until [...]
inputs.modified_text: This frames Israelis as a single, united public and treats continuing the war as the only serious form of protecting people. But security cannot mean asking civilians to absorb endless costs, and it cannot be built by ignoring the people on the other side who are also living with danger. Dismissing critics as distant also dodges the real question: whether this course protects lives or entrenches a cycle of harm. A just and durable security requires protecting everyone, listening to dissent, and confronting the political choices that keep the violence going—not simply pressing on.
